Can the police arrest me automatically: Whether police may arrest an accused as a matter of course on registration of an FIR for an offence under Section 498A IPC, or must be satisfied that arrest is necessary under Section 41 CrPC (arrest without warrant).
My neighbour filed a police case: Whether a dispute that is essentially civil in nature, concerning land or property, can be made the basis of a criminal complaint of cheating and forgery under the IPC, and when criminal proceedings may be quashed as an abuse of process.
Both parties have settled a case of grie: Whether a court can permit compounding of, or reduce the sentence in view of a compromise between the parties for, the offence of voluntarily causing grievous hurt, which is not compoundable under Section 320 CrPC.
The cheque bounced: Burden of proof and statutory presumptions under the Negotiable Instruments Act where a cheque is dishonoured and the drawer denies any legally enforceable debt or liability; Sections 138, 118 and 139.
Police searched me for drugs: Whether telling a person to be searched for narcotics that he may be searched before a Gazetted Officer or Magistrate, without clearly informing him of his right, satisfies the mandatory requirement of Section 50 of the NDPS Act.
They found drugs and say I must prove: Whether the burden of proof can be placed on the accused in a prosecution for possession of narcotic drugs under the NDPS Act: the presumption of culpable mental state under Section 35 and the standard of proof the accused must meet.
